motivation: Newcomers learn the ethical norms that are actually practiced in a workplace largely by watching how others handle ethically charged situations. For many people who began office-based careers in the early 2020s, a group that includes many members of Generation Z, that entry period took place partly at a distance, which may have changed what they learned and how durably.
problem: How does distributed (remote or hybrid) organizational entry change the transmission of a work unit's enacted ethical norms to newcomers, when can leaders offset the change, and do the effects persist after the entry period?
assumptions_explicit: Angle must differ from paper 1 and must not be generic.
One or two established theories; five to six propositions at most.
assumptions_inferred: Management/OB conceptual article genre, no target journal.
The Generation Z link should avoid unsupported value-difference claims (weak evidence) and instead rest on the timing of the cohort's career entry, stated as an assumption where not established.
constraints: Proposal mode (no numbers, no fabricated findings); every citation real and verified; one conceptual-model figure at most.
